canonical_definition: Refusal Behavior refers to the act of declining to generate responses to unsafe, harmful, or inappropriate inputs, such as malicious prompts, toxic/NSFW content, or jailbreaking attempts, often operationalized through explicit refusal to produce requested outputs. This behavior is commonly observed in safety-evaluated systems where it serves as an indicator of adherence to guardrails designed to prevent harmful content generation, with variants appearing in multimodal scenarios and adversarial contexts. It is typically framed as a safety capability but may also be treated as a task-compliance trait when contrasting coherent responses with refusals.
